newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Nepal diesel, kero import grows 14 pct, mulls term.
newsitem.headline: Nepal diesel, kero import grows 14 pct, mulls term.

text.p: Nepal's diesel and kerosene imports are growing at 14 percent a year and the country is studying the merits of buying on a term basis, an official with state-owned Nepal Oil Corp (NOC) said on Wednesday.
Nepal is expected to import 600,000 tonnes of diesel and kerosene in 20 cargoes this year, up from 18 cargoes last year, he said.
The import volume is equally divided between the two products.
Nepal started switching its imports to 0.5 percent sulphur diesel from the 1.0-percent grade about six months ago.
The official is in Singapore to meet middle-distillate traders from Shell, Vitol, Glencore, Mabanaft, BB Energy and Japan's Petrodiamond to discuss the benefits of initiating term purchase contracts.
NOC officials might also visit state-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp and the International Petroleum Group (IPG) in the Middle East later this year to explore the same issues, the official said.
Traders said NOC has been considering term purchases over the past three years but has so far not made a decision. They now buy through spot tenders issued on a monthly or bi-monthly basis.
"We are now more convinced about the benefits of a term contract but no decision has been made yet," said the official who declined to be named.
If a decision is made, NOC would take 60 percent of its imports by term contracts, which would be directly negotiated with selected suppliers, and the remainder by spot tenders, he said.
He said suppliers noted that term contracts would provide a stable source of supply and a fixed price throughout the year and protect the buyer from market fluctuations.
But traders noted that on the other hand, the buyer would not benefit from a sharp reduction in prices if they commit themselves to a fixed price.
Traders also said NOC are keen to assess the merits of buying spot cargoes on a free-on-board (fob) basis by chartering their own ships to take advantage of low freight rates.
This would mean that NOC might emulate the Indian Oil Corp (IOC) by tendering to buy on both cost-and-freight and fob basis. NOC now imports spot cargoes on a c-and-f basis.
